body_html:
How to think about it

Ohm's law: the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it at constant temperature, so V = IR. An ohmic conductor has a straight-line V–I graph; a light bulb filament is non-ohmic because its resistance rises as it heats up.

Electrical power is the rate at which electrical energy is converted: P = W/Δt = VI = I²R = V²/R. The energy used at home is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh): 1 kWh = 3,6 × 10⁶ J. Cost = energy (kWh) × price per kWh.

Example

A 230 V kettle draws 8 A. Power?

P = VI

Answer: 1 840 W

Example

A 2 kW heater runs for 3 h at R3 per kWh. Cost?

E = Pt in kWh

Answer: 6 kWh × R3 = R18

Common mistakes

  • Using P = I²R with the wrong current.
  • Mixing up kW and kWh.
  • Thinking a lamp filament is ohmic.

faq.q: Why does the resistance of a filament lamp increase?
faq.a: As it heats up, its atoms vibrate more and collide more with the electrons.

faq.q: Why is load shedding linked to power?
faq.a: When the total power demanded is more than power stations can supply, parts of the grid are switched off.
